incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: elevated 5xx from inference-gateway -> spike in model-runner OOM/segfaults. 5m error rate > 18%. Affected: prod-us-east models: redwood/gpt-medium, redwood/gpt-quant.
maya (oncall): seeing it, grabbing context. tagging runtime + sre. I'll take lead for now.
josh (runtime): on it. can someone paste the recent runner logs and a sample stacktrace? I want the failure signature (OOM vs segfault) and nvml events.
priya (sre): log link: https://infra.prod/logs?query=runner%20segfault&from=3412349000
priya (sre): small excerpt from gcagent: "CUDART: out of memory when allocating 136MB" then later a hard crash: "segfault at 0x0 in model_runner.cpp:482"
josh (runtime): good find. here's the stack we just pulled from a crashed core (abbreviated):
```
#0 0x7f8a3ac1 in kv_cache::get+0x1c model_runner.cpp:482
#1 0x7f8a3bcd in forward_attention+0x3a attention_kernel.cu:221
#2 0x7f8b7f2a in forward_pass model_executor.cc:113
#3 0x7f8c0012 in handle_request request_dispatcher.cc:78
```
josh (runtime): multiple crashes show both OOM allocation failures and null-deref in kv_cache path. hypothesis: overflowed cached pointers when batch sizes spike -> double-free/invalid pointer during eviction.
leo (eng-sre): dashboard: gateway latency + timeouts to clients are increasing. routing fallback not fully in place for these models.
sam (platform): we can flip gateway to fallback-model v2 for traffic to these model ids while we patch. command: `rbctl route update /v1/models/redwood/gpt-medium --fallback redwood/gpt-medium-v2 --drain 60s`
maya (oncall): do the reroute. priya, josh, watch rollback triggers. I'm going to page customers owner list.
priya (sre): applying reroute now.
priya (sre): `rbctl route update` returned 202, in progress. setting drain to 30s to reduce in-flight work.
carol (support): posting customer impact: 12 active customers saw transient 5xx in the last 10m, mostly short LLM API requests (chat completions). I'm sending status updates; will include mitigation note.
josh (runtime): while traffic shifts, we should reduce batch sizes and disable async prefetch to limit memory pressure. patch flags:
```
--max-batch=4
--kv-prefetch=false
```
josh (runtime): sending a hotpatch to the model runners in prod-us-east (canary first).
maya (oncall): please canary one host and confirm error rate for that host before wider rollout.
josh (runtime): canary applied to runner-23a, logs show no new OOMs in 60s. pushing to 5 more hosts.
priya (sre): metrics are responding: cluster OOM counter down from 17/min to 2/min after reroute + hotpatch.
tomo (observability): linking relevant traces: https://traces.prod/trace/0a1b2c - shows a correlation between large batch request bursts from a single client and the first failures.
leo (eng-sre): temporarily scaling dedicated pool to absorb excess load: +3 GPUs for prod-us-east. scaled via autoscaler override.
sam (platform): I've also disabled quantized kernel scheduling for gpt-quant variant until we confirm no memory corruption.
carol (support): update sent to customers: "We've applied a temporary traffic reroute and fixed an operational configuration to reduce memory pressure. Work is ongoing; we'll follow up once root cause confirmed." :white_check_mark:
maya (oncall): summary so far: 1) reroute traffic to fallback model, 2) hotpatch to reduce batch + disable kv-prefetch, 3) scale up capacity, 4) disable quant-kernel for suspect variant. Error rate dropped from 18% -> ~1.5% in 12 minutes. keeping incident open for RCA.
josh (runtime): saving core dumps and logs for postmortem. collecting `ulimit -c` outputs and ensuring symbols available.
priya (sre): starting live memory heap profiler on a subset of runners to catch object lifecycle around kv_cache eviction.
leo (eng-sre): customer-facing SLO impact estimate: ~0.3% p95 latency increase for the window, 12 customers impacted with short-term 5xx; no long-running jobs dropped.
carol (support): flagged enterprise accounts A and B for follow-up, contacting their CSMs now.
maya (oncall): next steps: josh and priya to lead debug and RCA, leo/sam to keep mitigation toggles ready, carol to maintain customer comms. I'll hand off to night-oncall at +4h unless resolved.
maya (oncall): @josh @priya please add a short post-incident doc in #postmortems when RCA done. I'll create the incident record now.
josh (runtime): ack. will include stack traces, core ids, and exact hotpatch diff.
priya (sre): ack. starting timeline and initial hypothesis in the incident doc.
incident-bot: Incident annotated: severity=sev2, incident_id=INC-2026-34123, responders=[maya, josh, priya, leo, sam, carol], state=mitigated -> monitoring.
maya (oncall): handing off to night team: @alex (oncall-night) you'll get briefed in 20m. leave mitigation toggles as-is unless error rate rises >3%.
carol (support): leaving notes for CSMs, will update Slack thread if any customers report repeats.
priya (sre): rolling debug window looks good. moving to evidence collection mode.
leo (eng-sre): thumbs up on followup plan. +1 on collecting binaries/symbols.
maya (oncall): thanks team. :thumbsup: closing live ops loop, keeping incident thread open for RCA additions."
